q: What is the difference between scaling up and scaling out?
a: Up = a bigger box (more concurrency in one server); out = more boxes (a balancer spreading load across small servers).

q: Why do both rows pass at 200 RPS?
a: Both sides have 320 RPS of capacity against 200 of load — headroom decides pass/fail, not the shape of the fleet.

q: What happens on both rows when you push to 300 RPS?
a: Both degrade together — p99 climbs steeply on each while verdicts still hold. Under even load, capacity is capacity; the shapes diverge under faults, not load.

q: When would you pick scale-out despite the extra moving part?
a: When one box cannot grow further, or when a dead backend must not take the system down — kill one thin server and three keep serving.
